metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 55), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.13-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
metrics.methodContext: Percent of the watershed in woody plus herbaceous wetland (NLCD 2019). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 55), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.13-provisional

curveCaveats: Built from 10 reference sites (exploratory band, below the automated floor of 20): the point value carries wide sampling error.
Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from Level I ecoregion 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests) because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 10 least-disturbed stations from Level I 8 (Eastern Temperate Forests), none of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level III, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is high and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

metrics.howToMeasure: Road density (km/sq km) is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good <1 km/km², Fair 1-<3 km/km², Poor ≥3 km/km².
metrics.methodContext: Road length per square kilometer of watershed. DEEP computes it for the delineated watershed. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
USDA Forest Service 2011, Watershed Condition Classification Technical Guide (FS-978)

limitations: Road density does not count actual outfalls or establish whether runoff is treated.
The 1 km/km² breakpoint is a screening judgment.

USFS watershed-condition guidance classes road density more strictly (good under 1, impaired over 2.4 miles per square mile, about 0.62 and 1.49 km/km²), derived from salmonid watersheds. EASI keeps the NRSA-anchored national screen and discloses the stricter alternative.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 55), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.13-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.
metrics.methodContext: Base flow index of the watershed, the percent of streamflow that comes from base flow (USGS base flow index grid). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

metrics.howToMeasure: Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
metrics.methodContext: Measure the thalweg depth at 10 or 15 evenly spaced stations between each pair of transects (100 or 150 along the reach). The scored candidates are benthic total taxa richness and native fish taxa richness, and native non-tolerant fish taxa richness was also tested under Pre-registration III. Too few comparable least-disturbed stations carry them in this ecoregion or in its Level II and Level I parents. On comparable national donors the strongest result was native non-tolerant fish taxa richness on distance-matched donors, which reached promising: its class calls agreed with reference in 16 of 19 evaluation regions with no systematic promotion, but its recovered thresholds fell inside the true answer's uncertainty in only 9 of 19, against the 13 required to validate. No modeled expectation passed validation under the extrapolation this ecoregion requires. Ohio EPA's ecoregional biocriteria, the nearest applicable published criterion, were checked on 2026-09-21 and are not usable here on three independent grounds. They set thresholds on composite indices (the fish Index of Biotic Integrity, the Modified Index of well-being, and the Invertebrate Community Index) rather than on taxa richness, so applying one to a richness count would compare different quantities. Those indices are computed under Ohio EPA's own field protocol against metric lines calibrated on Ohio reference sites, and the NRSA archive carries no index column and cannot derive one. They are Ohio water quality standards keyed to a per-waterbody use designation, while 26 of this ecoregion's 51 stations lie in Indiana. No suitable basis was found among the sources evaluated, which is not a finding that this function cannot be scored. No curve was forced and the function is reported as unassessed, so the ecosystem condition index is stated as an interval.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 16 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a parent ecoregion, stating the level and the transfer risk. 2 carry the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds no stream clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 2 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.
